levels.title: Potent Opioid Recognition
levels.description: Recognize high-potency synthetic opioids carrying catastrophic overdose risks.
levels.learningObjective: Differentiate fentaNYL and ALfentanil to prevent fatal opioid dosing errors.

activities.learningObjective: Recognize the target opioid medication name in realistic automated dispensing review scenarios.

questions.scenario: A patient order is received for a fentanyl transdermal patch. When searching the electronic medication cart, multiple synthetic opioid names appear.
questions.prompt: Which medication name matches the order and must be distinguished from the confusable counterpart ALfentanil?
questions.explanation: Fentanyl must be carefully selected to avoid confusion with ALfentanil and SUFentanil, which have dramatically different dosing potencies.

levels.title: Opioid Tall Man Discrimination
levels.description: Differentiate synthetic opioid prefixes and suffixes using ISMP Tall Man standards.
levels.learningObjective: Distinguish the correct ISMP Tall Man lettering standard for fentanyl and ALfentanil.

activities.learningObjective: Distinguish the correct ISMP Tall Man lettering standard for fentanyl.

questions.prompt: Which medication name correctly applies ISMP Tall Man lettering to differentiate fentanyl from ALfentanil?
questions.explanation: ISMP recommends fentaNYL (capitalizing the NYL suffix) to differentiate it from ALfentanil (capitalizing the AL prefix).

levels.title: Opioid Situational Verification
levels.description: Apply opioid Tall Man recognition in high-alert anesthesia and critical care orders.
levels.learningObjective: Accurately verify opioid orders under high-risk dispensing conditions.

activities.learningObjective: Verify the correct high-alert opioid in critical care dispensing.

questions.scenario: An intravenous anesthesia order is submitted specifying ALfentanil. The automated dispensing cabinet drawer also stores fentaNYL ampules.
questions.prompt: Which medication name correctly identifies the requested drug with its ISMP Tall Man designation?
questions.explanation: ALfentanil capitalizes AL to prevent mix-ups with fentaNYL, which has different pharmacokinetics and potency.

levels.title: Unit 4 Mastery
levels.description: Comprehensive review and unassisted Tall Man lettering mastery for High-Alert Opioids.
levels.learningObjective: Demonstrate complete unit mastery of opioid discrimination and unassisted Tall Man lettering without scaffolding.

activities.learningObjective: Review high-alert synthetic opioid differentiation under mastery conditions.

questions.prompt: Why does ISMP recommend capitalizing NYL in fentaNYL and AL in ALfentanil?
choices: To emphasize the distinct beginning and ending letter differences between the two drugs
To indicate that both drugs have the exact same dose
To denote pediatric versus adult formulations
To indicate oral versus injectable route
questions.correctAnswer: To emphasize the distinct beginning and ending letter differences between the two drugs
questions.explanation: ALfentanil emphasizes the prefix 'AL' while fentaNYL emphasizes the suffix 'NYL' to highlight their divergent orthographic segments.

activities.learningObjective: Independently construct the exact Tall Man lettering for fentanyl without scaffolding.

questions.prompt: UNIT MASTERY CAPSTONE TASK: Type the complete drug name using correct Tall Man lettering (capitalizing the specific distinguishing letters):
questions.explanation: fentaNYL capitalizes NYL to distinguish it from the closely related synthetic opioid ALfentanil.
